title: Two cars burn in vacant Rochester warehouse fire - NewsBreak
text: ROCHESTER, N.Y. (WROC) — Fire crews quickly brought a warehouse fire under control Tuesday evening after flames and heavy smoke were reported at a vacant building on Sherer Street near train tracks. According to the Rochester Fire Department, crews were dispatched just before 6 p.m. and found thick black smoke pouring from a one-story vacant warehouse. A working fire was declared. The structure was set back from the road and located near a set of train tracks, creating challenges for both access and water supply. Firefighters established a water supply by extending hoses from nearby street hydrants to trucks positioned closer to the building. Once inside, crews found two vehicles burning and began extinguishing the fire. For safety reasons, CSX was contacted and rail traffic in the area was halted for the duration of the response. The fire was under control within 20 minutes. No injuries were reported. The cause of the fire remains under investigation.
